newsitem.title: USA: Florida jobless rate dips to 5.1 pct in October.
newsitem.headline: Florida jobless rate dips to 5.1 pct in October.

text.p: Florida's unemployment rate dipped to 5.1 percent in October from 5.4 percent in September and 5.5 percent a year ago, the state Department of Labor and Employment Security said Tuesday.
The data represent 359,000 jobless Floridians out of a work force of 7.04 million. Total nonfarm employment was 6.2 million, up 169,000 jobs or 2.8 percent over the year.
Services added the most jobs over the year, 71,900, for a growth rate of 3.5 percent. Trade grew by 47,800 jobs or 3.1 percent.
Construction jobs gained 8,700 jobs over the year but remained far below the 1988-89 peak. Manufacturing jobs declined by 1,700 since last October, with all of the decline in nondurable goods.
The transportation, communications and public utilities sector grew by 8,300 jobs, or 2.7 percent. Finance, insurance and real estate gained 9,800 jobs, for 2.6 percent growth.
Government added 23,900 jobs over the year, for a growth rate of 2.5 percent, most of it in local government.

All of the state's metropolitan areas had over-the-year job increases. The Tampa-St. Petersburg area added the most, 27,200 jobs, while the Fort Lauderdale area had the fastest growth rate, 3.8 percent.
Liberty County had the lowest unemployment rate, 2.1 percent, while Hardee County had the highest, 17.1 percent.
